items.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: And this is where I got all my schooling, from these guys. Him and another trumpet player... these guys were all my teachers.

ctx.x: Well it must have been quite a challenge working with guys like Don Byas and so forth?

Oh man. Don Byas. One night he took a tune, and I’m glad I knew the tune, and he said, “Let’s go through the keys, Al.” I said, “Oh no.” He said, “Come on, man, you can—” I said, “I don’t even know it in this key.” But we went through all of the keys. And this is where I got all my schooling, from these guys. Him and another trumpet player, I forget his name now, but these guys were all my teachers. Not just one person, I had several teachers you know. I learned from several people.
And it wasn’t even like official lessons, it was just like on the job, right?
